Inverting IRIS Observations with MART#

The main target of ESIS-I is the \(\text{O\,V}\;630\,\AA\) spectral line. To our knowledge, high-quality spectroheliograms of this line are not available to use as a test dataset. The Coronal Diagnostic Spectrometer (CDS) [Harrison et al., 1996] and the Solar Ultraviolet Measurements of Emitted Radiation (SUMER) [Wilhelm et al., 1995] have both observed this line, but their spatial or spectral resolution is not sufficient to use as a test for ESIS (but see Landi et al. [2000] for a possible SUMER candidate). Instead, we will use observations of the \(\text{Si\,IV}\;1394\,\AA\) spectral line from the Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS) [De Pontieu et al., 2014] as a proxy for the \(\text{O\,V}\;630\,\AA\) line. These observations will be used along with a simple model of the ESIS instrument to create synthetic ESIS images. We will then use MART to invert these images and test how well it recovers the original scene.

Loading the Test Scene#

Load an IRIS observation to use as a test scene to invert. This function shifts and scales the \(\text{Si\,IV}\;1394\,\AA\) spectral line observed by IRIS to match the \(\text{O\,V}\;630\,\AA\) line observed by ESIS.

Defining a Model of the ESIS Instrument#

In this tutorial we’ll use an idealized version of the ESIS instrument model that considers only dispersion and shot noise.

We’ll start by saving the rest wavelength of the \(\text{O\,V}\;630\,\AA\) line.

[9]:

Use the rest wavelength to define an astropy.units equivalency for converting between Doppler velocities and wavelength units.

coordinates_degraded = na.TemporalDopplerPositionalVectorArray.from_velocity(
    time=scene.inputs.time.mean(scene.axis_detector_x),
    velocity=velocity_degraded,
    wavelength_rest=wavelength_rest,
    position=position_degraded,
)

[31]:

scene_degraded = ctis.regrid(
    coordinates_input=scene.inputs,
    coordinates_output=coordinates_degraded,
    values_input=scene.outputs,
    axis_wavelength=scene.axis_wavelength,
    axis_position=(scene.axis_detector_x, scene.axis_detector_y),
)
scene_degraded = scene.replace(
    inputs=coordinates_degraded,
    outputs=scene_degraded,
)

Invert synthetic ESIS images#

Now for the tricky part, inverting these images into a reconstructed scene using MART.

An important part of using MART effectively is the initial guess supplied to the algorithm. In this case we will be decomposing the guess into separable spatial and spectral components. The spatial component will be found by constructing the “poor man’s zeroth order image”, which is found by projecting each ESIS image onto the skyplane and then taking the minimum along the channel axis.

std_OV = esis.flights.f1.spectrum.O_V.width_doppler
v = scene_degraded.inputs.velocity.cell_centers(scene.axis_wavelength)
# guess_spectral = np.exp(-np.square(v / std_OV) / 2)
std_OV = 37.5  * 1.5 * u.km / u.s
kappa = 0.2
v0 = 0 * u.km / u.s
guess_spectral = (1 + np.square((v - v0) / std_OV) / kappa)**(-kappa - 1)
guess_spectral = guess_spectral / guess_spectral.sum()

    colorbar = na.plt.rgbmesh(
        scene_degraded.inputs.velocity.cell_centers(scene.axis_wavelength),
        scene_degraded.inputs.position.x,
        scene_degraded.inputs.position.y,
        C=solution.outputs,
        axis_wavelength=scene.axis_wavelength,
        ax=ax2,
        vmin=vmin,
        vmax=vmax,
        wavelength_min=-250 * u.km / u.s,
        wavelength_max=+250 * u.km / u.s,
    )
    na.plt.pcolormesh(
        C=colorbar,
        axis_rgb=scene.axis_wavelength,
        ax=cax,
    )
    ax1.set_title("degraded")
    ax2.set_title("reconstructed")
    unit_x = scene_degraded.inputs.position.x.unit
    unit_y = scene_degraded.inputs.position.y.unit
    ax1.set_xlabel(f"scene $x$ ({unit_x:latex_inline})")
    ax2.set_xlabel(f"scene $x$ ({unit_x:latex_inline})")
    ax1.set_ylabel(f"scene $y$ ({unit_y:latex_inline})")
    cax.xaxis.set_ticks_position("top")
    cax.xaxis.set_label_position("top")
    cax.yaxis.tick_right()
    cax.yaxis.set_label_position("right")
